news.title: Gianni Infantino: UEFA signs joint letter slamming 'deception' at top of FIFA as World Cup stake sale fallout continues
news.lede: UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC have hit out at "deception" and a "fundamental breach of trust" around Gianni Infantino's botched World Cup stake sale plans to further raise the pressure on the under-fire FIFA president. The three continental associations each signed a new open letter to the "football family" on Monday, without naming Infantino specifically but referring to a leader who "abandoned their duty" by breaking trust "through deception". In the three-page document they again criticised the president's World Cup sale plans and rejected FIFA's claim that they had been a "mistake", adding: "There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment - not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."

news.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
news.lede: Confederations write open letter damning Fifa president. Concacaf president Montagliani seen as top contender. Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”. In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

news.title: Women's World Cup 2027: Nigeria 'still have hope' after Wafcon 2026 exit
news.lede: Nigeria's quarter-final exit at Wafcon 2026 is their worst performance at the finals, with the defending champions previously lifting the trophy 10 times in total. Goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie says Nigeria have to "go back to the drawing board" after missing out on automatic qualification for the 2027 Fifa Women's World Cup. The Super Falcons failed to reach the semi-finals of the ongoing 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) in Morocco, falling to a 1-0 defeat by Cameroon in the last eight on Sunday. By reaching the last four, Cameroon have now guaranteed a ticket to next year's World Cup in Brazil alongside fellow semi-finalists Algeria, Malawi and Morocco.

news.title: UEFA, AFC and CONCACAF slam FIFA President Infantino over World Cup stake sale
news.lede: Infantino has been the butt of scathing criticism ever since launching, and then withdrawing within days, a plan to bring in private investment into FIFA competitions, including the World Cups. news.title: Three Tottenham players set to return to training as Cristian Romero decision made
news.lede: Cristian Romero, Pedro Porro and Djed Spence are set to return to Tottenham this week to meet back up with Roberto De Zerbi and their team-mates. Porro returns as a World Cup winner, having starred at the competition with Spain and beaten Romero's Argentina in the final. The right-back was named in the team of the tournament and ensured it was the third consecutive World Cup that a Tottenham player emerged as a winner after Hugo Lloris and Romero triumphed in 2018 and 2022 respectively.

news.title: Man Utd and Arsenal set asking price for new transfer target Joaquin Seys
news.lede: Joaquin Seys is catching the eye of a lot of big clubs (Picture: Getty Images) Arsenal and Manchester United are among the many admirers of Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys and they now know how much he will cost. The 21-year-old has become a regular for his club side, already racking up 97 first team appearances in all competitions. 23 of those games have come in the Champions League, so he has been competing at the elite level, also picking up six caps for Belgium and playing at the World Cup this summer. There is little surprise that big clubs have come calling and the Red Devils and Gunners are not the only ones who have taken note. The Sun report that Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also been tracking his progress, while Porto and Benfica have also been touted as interested parties.

news.title: Training Report: Bayern Munich injured stars almost ready; World Cup contingent out a little longer; and MORE!
news.lede: It has been a busy few days for Bayern Munich when it comes to personnel news. News that emerged on Sunday from Säbener Straße indicated that Bayern Munich stars Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala could be back in team training this week (per Bild via @iMiaSanMia): > Among the players currently recovering from injury, Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala are the most advanced in their rehab. Both are expected back in team training at the beginning of the coming week [@BILD] In addition, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia) is reporting that Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano are getting more time off and will not be fully back in action until next week: > Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano have been given more vacation time and won’t return to Munich until the end of the coming week.
